root_idea.summary: The root centers on gathering, enclosing, holding back, and preventing movement or access.
root_idea.development: From enclosure and restraint, the root develops meanings of besieging, detention, inward constriction, abstention, and related senses involving things brought together or held within boundaries.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized Form I citation forms حَصَرَ / حَصِرَ, covering the supplied transitive and intransitive Quranic uses.
Displayed under the normalized Form IV perfect citation form أَحْصَرَ.
Displayed as the nominal citation form حَصِير.
Displayed as the nominal/adjectival citation form حَصُور.

senses.definition: To surround, hem in, besiege, or confine someone, thereby restricting movement or access.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic imperative in 9:5 describes surrounding and besieging people. The transitive use may include preventing a person or group from proceeding freely.

senses.definition: To become inwardly constricted, shrinking from or being unable to undertake an action.
senses.usage_conditions: In 4:90 the constriction is predicated of the bosoms of people who are reluctant or unable to fight. This is an inward state of inhibition, distinct from an external siege.

senses.definition: To be prevented, detained, or held back from proceeding or reaching a destination.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic passive construction includes being prevented from pilgrimage or from pursuing one's course by an external obstacle or an internal cause such as illness. It also describes people confined in the path of God.
In 17:8, the term is interpreted as a prison or other place that confines; the interpretation treats it as something that holds people in.

senses.definition: A woven mat, bed, or spread laid out for sitting or lying.
senses.usage_conditions: In 17:8, an alternative interpretation understands the word as a mat or bed, including a woven spread placed on the ground.

senses.definition: Sexually abstinent; one who does not have sexual intercourse with women.
senses.usage_conditions: In 3:39 the term describes John. Classical explanations include abstention through chastity and abstention through impotence; the chaste abstention is presented as the more fitting Quranic interpretation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be held back from journeying or a desired act by illness, fear, or another internal impediment; to restrain oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the internally caused or self-restraining branch, distinguished in some accounts from being forcibly confined by another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take the whole of something, appropriate it exclusively, or acquire it for oneself.
Suppression of the feces or constipation of the bowels; in some usage, suppression of urine as well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The terminology is distinguished in some authorities from a separate term for urinary suppression, while others extend it to both.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Afflicted with suppression of the feces or constipation of the bowels, and sometimes with suppression of urine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the passive adjectival description of a person suffering the condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel: to have a narrow orifice to the teat, or for that orifice to become narrow.
Of a she-camel: having a narrow orifice to the teat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an animal-specific adjectival use, separate from the Quranic description of a sexually abstinent person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Suppression of a camel's milk flow, associated with heaviness or heaving of the stomach, a tendency to vomit, or unwillingness to yield milk.
A she-camel whose flow of milk is suppressed.
To be unable to express one's meaning, falter in speech, or become impeded in reading or recitation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The impediment may arise from shame, confusion, or another accidental cause; it is not simply a pronunciation or grammatical defect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person unable to express what he wishes to say, or unable to proceed in reading or recitation.
To abstain from sexual intercourse or be prevented from having it, despite the capacity or desire for it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may refer to voluntary abstention or to impotence; it is a Classical verbal construction distinct from the Quranic adjectival form حَصُورٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To vomit.
To become affected by a disease or malady.
To be niggardly, tenacious, penurious, or avaricious.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The use may describe refusing to spend on companions or withholding one's contribution to a shared occasion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A niggardly, withholding, or avaricious person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may describe one who refuses to spend on drinking companions or take part in a customary game because of stinginess.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To conceal a secret or refrain from divulging it.
A strict concealer of secrets.
To bind or fit a حِصَار or similar pad and saddle apparatus onto a camel.
To become restrained, withheld, or prevented.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the intransitive Form VII usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse: sexually impotent or unable to mate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This animal application is distinct from the Quranic human description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Castrated; having the penis and testicles amputated.
Very fearful or cautious, refraining from an action through fear.
A woman whose sexual passage is impervious to intercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an anatomical description, synonymous in the cited evidence with رَتْقَاءُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A maker or seller of reed, rush, or palm-leaf mats.
A fortress, fort, or castle.
A padded camel saddle, cushion, pad, or small saddle apparatus placed or bound upon a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term covers several closely related forms of padding or saddle equipment used by riders or animal trainers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Straitened, surrounded, besieged, beset, confined, detained, or prevented from journeying.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the passive adjectival form, including confinement within or by a fortress.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel furnished with a حِصَار or related saddle pad.
A king or ruler.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The title is explained either by the ruler's seclusion or by his preventing unrestricted access to him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woven thing, especially a mat made from reeds, rushes, papyrus, or palm leaves.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural forms include حُصُرٌ and the contracted حُصْرٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An ornamented or variegated garment or piece of cloth whose beauty captivates the heart when spread out.
A sitting-place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This sense is reported in the lexical evidence, though one comment regards it as possibly a textual error for a place of confinement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The surface of the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The mat sense is explained in relation to something spread over the ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited explanation may relate the term to the woven or rippled appearance of a surface.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The diversified wavy marks, streaks, or grain of a sword; also one of the sword's two sides in a related use.
A road or way.
A row of men or of other things.
A side of the body, or the transverse vein, sinew, or portion of flesh extending across the side of a camel, horse, or other beast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The anatomical descriptions vary between the visible side, the transverse vein, adjoining sinew, and the flesh between the ribs and flank.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place in which dates are dried.

cautions: Form I uses include active surrounding or confinement and an intransitive inward constriction; the supplied evidence also records differing Classical accounts of the distinction between حَصَرَ and أَحْصَرَ.
حَصِيرٌ in 17:8 has materially different supported interpretations: a prison or confining enclosure, and a woven mat or bed.
حَصُورٌ in 3:39 is explained either as abstention through chastity or as impotence; the chastity interpretation is favored in the Quran-focused evidence.
The reported sitting-place sense of حَصِيرٌ is accompanied by a lexicographic qualification that it may be an error for a place of confinement.
